paragraphs: Children in care in Leicester are looked after by carers approved by Leicester City Council, which describes its service as one of the largest fostering services in the East Midlands, and by the independent agencies listed on this page. In May 2026, during Foster Care Fortnight, the council said it urgently needs more foster carers in the city. It pointed out that when there are not enough local carers, children can be placed away from Leicester, far from their family, friends, school and clubs.

The council recruits for several kinds of care, including kinship fostering for relatives and family friends, and runs regular information sessions for people who want to find out more before applying. Its Foster Care Fortnight appeal featured a Leicester family who have fostered together for more than 30 years.

Leicester pays a weekly amount for each child by age, from £182 for children aged up to 4 to £267 for young people aged 16 and over. On top of this it pays a weekly accreditation payment for each child, starting at £50 for newly approved carers and rising to £90 for established carers, £250 for enhanced fostering and £440 for specialist fostering. Carers also receive extra weeks of allowance for birthdays, festivals and holidays. Our Leicester allowance page has the details.
If you are thinking about fostering in Leicester, speak to the council and to the agencies below, go to an information session, and ask each service about training, support and pay before you decide.

sources.title: Urgent need for foster carers in Leicester (Leicester City Council news, 13 May 2026)
